BEYOND THE SCREEN

Look up.
Your next discovery is outside.

A clear evening, a darker place, and a little patience are enough to begin.

A CHANGE IN PERSPECTIVE

Every star you see
is a message from the past.

Moonlight takes about 1.3 seconds to reach us. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes.
The farther we look, the further back in time we see.

ONE LIGHT-YEAR ≈ 9.46 TRILLION KILOMETRESCOSMIC CLIFFS · JAMES WEBB SPACE TELESCOPE

TAKE YOUR CURIOSITY OUTSIDE

Your next lab?
The night sky.

No telescope needed for a first discovery.

01

Find a darker corner.

Choose a clear evening and move away from streetlights. Less artificial light reveals more stars.

02

Let your eyes adjust.

Give your eyes around 20–30 minutes in the dark. Keep bright phone screens tucked away.

03

Start with the Moon.

Follow its changing shape over several nights. Binoculars reveal detail along the boundary between light and shadow.

Observe safely: never look at the Sun through binoculars or a telescope without a proper solar filter fitted over the front.
